## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Most of this PR is mechanical and safe, but one change breaks behavior. The typing and `log.warn`→`log.warning` edits across the 180 `*_records.py` handlers are pure replacements, and `by_name` behaves the same with `itemgetter`. The rewrite of `requirement_proven` does not: it flips the result for an empty criteria list, even though the PR body says "No behavior change is intended."

## Critical
- app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:12 — correctness — Before this change, `requirement_proven([])` returned `False` because of `bool(criteria) and all(...)`. It now computes `proven = sum(...)`, which is `0`, and returns `0 == len([])`, which is `True`. The `if not criteria:` branch at line 9 only logs a warning and then falls through. No test catches this: `tests/test_handlers.py:17-19` only covers non-empty lists. Could you restore the empty check, for example `return bool(criteria) and proven == len(criteria)` or `return bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`, and add `assert not requirement_proven([])`? — In release review, a requirement with no criteria at all will now be reported as proven, so an unverified requirement can pass review.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `by_name` keeps its old behavior: `itemgetter("name")` returns the same key as `lambda row: row["name"]` and raises the same `KeyError` when the key is missing. `tests/test_handlers.py:13-14` covers it.
- In all 180 `app/handlers/h*_records.py` files, the only changes are removing `from typing import Dict, List`, switching to built-in generics in the six `step_N` signatures, and replacing `log.warn` with `log.warning`. I confirmed this by counting lines in the pinned diff. There are 2,160 added lines, which is 180 files × 12. There are 2,341 removed lines: 180 files × 13 = 2,340, plus the typing import removed from `h091_requirements.py`. The leftover added and removed lines all belong to `h040_sorting.py`, `h091_requirements.py` and `review.txt`.

## Not reviewed
- I only read `app/handlers/h000_records.py` and `app/handlers/h001_records.py` line by line in the diff. For the other 178 records files (`app/handlers/h002_records.py` through `app/handlers/h179_records.py`), I checked the diff hunks with the line-pattern counts above, not by reading each one. I did not open any of the head-side files except `app/handlers/h091_requirements.py`.
- The repository has no Python version declaration (no `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg` or similar), so I could not confirm that the target runtime is Python 3.9 or later. Built-in generics such as `list[dict[str, int]]` in annotations need 3.9+.
